title: Introduction
excerpt: Relay is a Claude Code plugin for autonomous feature delivery: a single prompt drives the full cycle from PRD to merged PR via orchestrated writer/reviewer agent pairs and a Test Runner that closes the loop.

title: Installation
excerpt: Clone the repo, enable the marketplace in Claude Code, verify the skill loads. No npm install, no build step. Prerequisites: Claude Code, Node 18+, Git. Docker and gh CLI recommended.

title: First run
excerpt: Walk through invoking the context-builder for the first time: the nine phases it runs, the final report to read, validating [INFERRED - VALIDATE] items, answering open questions, required .gitignore entries.

title: The three pillars
excerpt: Relay's pipeline is organized in three pillars: Initialization (context-builder), Implementation (PRD to PR, including implement-time docs-sync), and Approval (merge plus a low-delta docs-sync safety net). Each pillar has a clear boundary.

title: Interactivity boundary
excerpt: The pipeline is interactive up to PRD approval and autonomous from there on. Catching misunderstanding at PRD time costs minutes; fixing it after implementation costs hours.

title: Pipeline stages
excerpt: Writer/reviewer pairs plus the Test Runner. Each stage has a specific input, output, and recovery path. This page walks through all eight stages and their per-stage retry budgets.

title: TDD opt-in
excerpt: TDD is an explicit opt-in via docs/context/methodology.md with tdd: true. Heuristic activation is forbidden — explicit declaration only. When active, tests are written before implementation by the TDD Writer. Foundation phases (phase_type: foundation) skip test-first in compiled languages (Java/JUnit, Go, .NET) so the seam can be created first.

title: PRP artifact paths
excerpt: Pipeline artifacts (PRDs, plans, reports, reviews) live under PRPs/ at the repo root, never under .claude/. The only .claude/ write is settings.json during context-builder setup.

title: Graceful degradation
excerpt: Every component detects its preconditions at start. Missing infrastructure results in a clear skip with a reason — never a silent failure, never a crash. No Docker, no tests, no GitHub — each case has defined behavior.

title: Writing a PRD
excerpt: Walkthrough of the /relay-prd interactive flow: when to write one, the 6-phase Q&A (initiate, foundation, grounding, deep dive, technical, decisions), writing good acceptance criteria, the reviewer loop, status approval.

title: Running tests
excerpt: How to use /relay-test directly — standalone Test Runner with auto-correction. Invocation flags, interpreting verdict codes (GREEN, FAILED_*), reading the report, the current /relay-implement gap.

title: Validation suite
excerpt: The plugin's own self-test: npm run validate runs twelve static consistency checks and npm run eval checks the reviewer agents against golden fixtures. Why it exists, why it is built this way, how to run it, cost, and how to maintain it.

title: Handling failures
excerpt: What to do when the pipeline aborts. Per-outcome recovery: retry exhaustion, time budget, oscillation, unrecoverable infra (missing settings.json, Docker down, DB unreachable, normalizer failure, no test framework).

title: Post-green review
excerpt: After GREEN, run /relay-test-review to verify tests weren't weakened. Four concern types: removed tests, added skips, trivial assertions, coverage drops. How to set up the optional coverage baseline.

title: Troubleshooting
excerpt: Known issues and concrete fixes: installation (plugin not visible, node not found, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT), context-builder (inferred items, domain areas), permissions (prompts, gitignore), Docker, reporting, secrets.

title: Commands
excerpt: Nineteen commands, no placeholder. Orchestrator /relay-execute composes /relay-plan, /relay-plan-review, /relay-worktree, /relay-write-test, /relay-test-write-review, /relay-implement, /relay-code-review, /relay-test, and /relay-test-review end to end. All Pillar 3 commands shipped: /relay-commit (v0.14.0), /relay-pr (v0.15.0), /relay-approve (v0.17.0). /relay-qa-report (v0.20.0) is the QA / Support command in the human validation gate. /relay-plan supports a description-only (PRD-less) mode in addition to the standard APPROVED-PRD mode. Full command surface by role: writers, reviewers, infra, orchestrator, QA / Support, and Pillar 3. /relay-visual-approve is the standalone, human-triggered infra command serving the Figma Visual-First Track's human-mode visual approval gate, never invoked by /relay-execute.

title: Agents
excerpt: Specialized Claude Code agents invoked by commands. Implemented: test-runner, post-green-reviewer, prd-writer, prd-reviewer, research-web, research-codebase, plan-writer, plan-reviewer, implementer, code-reviewer, code-reviewer-semantic, test-writer, test-reviewer, docs-updater (dispatched twice, implement-time primary and approve-time safety net, v0.17.0), docs-reviewer (dispatched twice, implement-time primary and approve-time safety net, v0.17.0). Each has focused prompt, narrow tool allowlist, structured output.

title: Skills
excerpt: Claude Code skills loaded on demand. relay ships one: context-builder. Initializes a target project's docs tree, permission allowlist, methodology declaration, and the mandatory test guardrail (testing.md + CLAUDE.md) that keeps e2e and other suites green on every change.

title: Scripts
excerpt: Helper scripts written in Node.js with zero npm dependencies. normalize-test-output.mjs (JUnit XML to canonical schema) and generate-final-report.mjs (assembles the PR-embeddable markdown report).

title: Validation checks
excerpt: Complete per-check catalog of the validation suite: for each of the twelve static checks and the eval layer, the functionality guarded, a passing example, a failing example with the verbatim finding text, and the covering unit tests (166 total).

title: Test output schema
excerpt: Canonical JSON schema v1 every test framework output is normalized into. Produced by normalize-test-output.mjs; consumed by B3 classifier and B4 auto-correction loop. Field reference and framework-specific mappings.

title: Settings allowlist
excerpt: Narrow permission patterns per stack signal plus an invariant denylist. Emitted by context-builder into the target project's .claude/settings.json. Broad patterns like Bash(*) are forbidden.

title: Redaction policy
excerpt: Three-layer secret redaction: invariant defaults (env name wildcards + exact URL vars + value regex for AWS/Stripe/GitHub/JWT/PEM/OpenAI/Anthropic/Google), per-project extensions, documented non-redacted values.

title: QA report
excerpt: The /relay-qa-report human validation gate command: four-way argument router (PRD, plan, description, diff mode), seven-field per-case schema, honesty guarantee for uncovered cases, record.json coverage grounding, anti-overwrite and FAILED_NOTHING_TO_REPORT HALTs.

title: /relay-design-map
excerpt: Build or refresh docs/design/component-map.md — a versioned, human-curatable map from Figma library components to real code components. Queries the Figma library in the main session, persists evidence to PRPs/reports/design-map/evidence/, dispatches the design-map-writer/design-map-reviewer pair in a bounded retry loop, runs a preflight report, then asks for explicit confirmation before flipping figma_track: true. Part of the Figma Implementation Track (Phase 3).

title: design-map-writer
excerpt: Writer agent invoked by /relay-design-map. Reads persisted Figma evidence plus the local design-system clone and writes docs/design/component-map.md conforming to the canonical component-map-template.md shape. Never queries the Figma MCP directly; never approves its own output.

title: design-map-reviewer
excerpt: Reviewer agent invoked by /relay-design-map after design-map-writer. Validates a DRAFT component-map.md against the seven-item R-DM1-R-DM7 rubric (import-path resolution, evidence cross-reference, prop/variant existence, duplicate-id guard, honest inventory_truncated scoping, non-empty Conventions, honest enrichment_truncated scoping) and owns the DRAFT-to-APPROVED flip. MCP-free.

title: /relay-design-spec
excerpt: Turn a Figma URL into a human-approved, business-grounded Design Spec. Adopts design-spec-writer then design-spec-reviewer inline in the main conversation (never Task-dispatched), performing all Figma MCP querying itself. Writes PRPs/designs/<feature>/design-spec.md; flips to APPROVED only after the user's own explicit affirmative reply. Part of the Figma Implementation Track (Phase 4).

title: design-spec-writer
excerpt: Writer agent inline-adopted by /relay-design-spec (never Task-dispatched). Interprets a Figma URL into a business-grounded Design Spec via restate-and-wait confirmation, chunked persist-then-discard MCP traversal, component-map-lensed REUSE/NEW/AMBIGUOUS classification, and a bounded batched Q&A round. Never approves its own output.

title: design-spec-reviewer
excerpt: Reviewer agent inline-adopted by /relay-design-spec (never Task-dispatched) with invocation_context: main. Validates a DRAFT design-spec.md against the seven-item R-DS1-R-DS7 rubric, MCP-free, and owns the human-confirmed DRAFT-to-APPROVED flip after the user's own explicit affirmative reply.

title: research-design
excerpt: Third grounding subagent invoked by plan-writer during Phase 2 GROUNDING, alongside research-codebase and research-web, only when a design_spec_path is available (design_source: figma). Verifies every CM-<n> id a Design Spec's Component Mapping cites still resolves against docs/design/component-map.md and the design-system clone, flags stale mappings, and harvests real usage snippets for the plan's own Patterns to Mirror section. Text-only; never queries the Figma MCP; never reads image files. Part of the Figma Implementation Track (Phase 5).

title: visual-verifier
excerpt: Dispatched non-interactively by /relay-implement's Phase A.3.4 (Visual-verification dispatch), immediately after code-review APPROVED, AND by the standalone /relay-visual-review command. Orchestrates the self-contained plugins/relay/scripts/visual/ tooling (provision -> capture -> compare) against a plan's ## Design Source table and the referenced APPROVED Design Spec's ## Visual Acceptance Criteria table, writes fidelity-report.json, and returns VISUAL_VERIFIED, VISUAL_DEGRADED, or VISUAL_MISMATCH. Degrades gracefully through DEGRADED_STATIC_ONLY / DEGRADED_PROVISION_FAILED rungs rather than blocking delivery; never edits application code; never queries the Figma MCP. Part of the Figma Implementation Track (Phase 6; dispatcher extended in Phase 7).

title: /relay-visual-review
excerpt: Standalone, single-shot, non-mutating re-check of visual fidelity for a plan whose ## Metadata carries design_source: figma. Dispatches the visual-verifier agent exactly once (attempt: 1 sentinel, mirroring /relay-code-review's dispatch shape), surfaces VISUAL_VERIFIED / VISUAL_DEGRADED / VISUAL_MISMATCH plus the fidelity-report.json path, and performs zero D8 mutations. Part of the Figma Implementation Track (Phase 7).

title: /relay-visual-approve
excerpt: Standalone, human-triggered infra command recording the Figma Visual-First Track's human-mode visual-approval decision. Locates the single unresolved AWAITING_VISUAL_APPROVAL halt for a feature, surfaces the fidelity report plus captured/reference screenshot paths, requires explicit confirmation, and flips the phase's halt.json plus an appended visual-approval.jsonl audit line. Never invoked by /relay-execute. Part of the Figma Visual-First Track (Phase 6).

title: Decisions
excerpt: Stable technical decisions that must not be re-evaluated by the AI. Each entry includes context, decision, reason, and affected areas. 14 decisions documented as of 2026-04-21.

title: Anti-patterns
excerpt: Forbidden patterns and intentional restrictions. The AI must not implement anything listed here, even when it seems correct.

title: Decision Gate
excerpt: Mandatory cognitive control mechanism activated before planning, coding, or review. Forces consultation of decisions.md, anti-patterns.md, architecture, constraints, methodology, and domain areas. Evidence block, halt conditions, exemptions.

title: Phase status
excerpt: Overall rollout across 5 phases: Foundation, Testing, Agents, Approval, CI/CD. Plus per-PRD phase status for the Test Runner — 8 of 9 phases complete.

title: Test Runner PRD
excerpt: Deep dive into the 9-phase PRD that delivered the Test Runner: foundations, infra primitives, normalizer, classifier, auto-correction loop, post-green reviewer, report, TDD track, dogfood. Per-phase acceptance criteria.

title: Phoenix dogfood
excerpt: First target project used to validate the plugin end-to-end on 2026-04-21. Synthetic JUnit XML run against the real normalizer and report generator. Artifacts walkthrough (run.json, record.json, test-review.json, final-report.md), four issues surfaced and fixed.

title: Changelog
excerpt: History of every user-visible change to the documentation site. Independent semver from the relay plugin. Entries follow Keep a Changelog: Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed. Retroactive entries for releases 0.1 through 0.5.
